newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Korean borrowers in spotlight.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Korean borrowers in spotlight.

text.p: South Korean borrowers Pohang Iron and Steel (Posco) and Korea Long Term Credit Bank enlivened Asian debt markets on Wednesday.
Posco has a US$200 million unsecured Yankee bond in the works that is expected to be priced later tonight in New York via lead manager JP Morgan.
Bankers in Hong Kong said the issue is likely to have a maturity of seven years.
Moody's Investors Service today assigned an A2 rating to Posco's Yankee, a notch lower than South Korea's A1 sovereign rating.
Last October, Posco launched a ten-year fixed rate Yankee at a spread of 70 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Though the note is currently traded at 98/102 basis points over the benchmark, it has tightened "by a few basis points over the past two weeks," one trader said
In general, Korean credits have not performed well this year, suffering as did the rest of Korea's financial sector following the default of Hanbo Steel, the second largest steel maker in Korea.
"Korean paper is certainly on an tightening track," one syndicate manager said.
Bankers said market's appetite for Korean credits has been improving as the country's latest economic indicators showed signs of recovery.
A3-rated Korea Long Term Credit Bank today launched a step-up floating rate note issue into Asian debt markets.

The facility has a final maturity of three years with annual put options. It pays an all-in return of 43 basis points to the first put, 48.5 basis points second put and 52 basis points if held to maturity.
Despite the increasing interest for Korean paper, some bankers said at 52 basis points for three years, the pricing on the Korean Long-Term deal is tight.
The borrower's outstanding three-year paper is trading at 70 basis points in secondary market, they said.
"There is only limited appetite for Korean paper with tenors longer than one year," a Japanese banker said.
In other news, Standard and Poor's Corp raised the ratings Polysindo Eka Perkas and one of its unit's to BB-plus from BB.
In New York, market sources in New York said bond investors' sentiment towards Thailand was cautiously optimistic.
"If Thailand were to issue bonds now, they would sell well," said a syndicate manager.
But investors would ask for a higher risk premium now, the syndicate manager said.
Thailand plans to raise US$10 billion through bank borrowing and bond issuance to replenish its reserves, severely depleted during its defence against speculative attacks on its currency.
-- Angi Li Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2847 4039
